mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals monetary easing, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases but SPX 20-day returns are not positive in most cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate indicates a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises but SPX returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in housing starts suggests reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST drops below 1500 but SPX 60-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment and employment together indicate labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE and PAYEMS rise but SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows but SPX 60-day returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production suggests supply constraints, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops below 112 but SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation with static interest rates may lead to decreased purchasing power, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises but FEDFUNDS don't adjust and SPX returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS grows but SPX 20-day returns are not positive.
